constructors.tooltip:
Creates a Spark Max and resets it to its default settings, so that it only has the
    settings that the robot code gives it.

    :param can_port:  The CAN bus that the Spark Max is connected to.
    :param device_id: The CAN device id of the Spark Max.
    :param type:      The kind of motor connected to the Spark Max. NEO motors are brushless.

instanceMethods.tooltip: Clears all sticky faults.

Set the configuration for the SPARK without waiting for a response.

If @c resetMode is ResetMode::kResetSafeParameters, this
method will reset safe writable parameters to their default values before
setting the given configuration. The following parameters will not be
reset by this action: CAN ID, Motor Type, Idle Mode, PWM Input Deadband,
and Duty Cycle Offset.

If @c persistMode is PersistMode::kPersistParameters, this
method will save all parameters to the SPARK's non-volatile memory after
setting the given configuration. This will allow parameters to persist
across power cycles.

NOTE: This method will immediately return REVLibError::kOk and the
action will be done in the background. Any errors that occur will be
reported to the driver station.

:param config:       The desired SPARK configuration
:param reset_mode:   Whether to reset safe parameters before setting the
                     configuration
:param persist_mode: Whether to persist the parameters after setting the
                     configuration

:returns: REVLibError::kOk
          @see Configure()

Gives this Spark Max all of the settings that another Spark Max has been given, like its
    idle mode, current limit, and PID gains, so that a group of motors can be set up by setting
    up one of them. Settings that the other Spark Max hasn't been given stay the way they are on
    this one. Which Spark Max it follows isn't copied, and neither is set_inverted, since motors
    in a group often turn opposite ways.

    :param other: The Spark Max to copy the settings of.

the alternate encoder mode data port pins. These are defined as:

Pin 4 (Forward Limit Switch): Index
Pin 6 (Multi-function): Encoder A

This call will disable support for the limit switch inputs.

NOTE: Follower mode will start automatically upon configuring follower
mode. If the SPARK experiences a power cycle and has follower mode
configured, follower mode will automatically restart. This method is only
useful after PauseFollowerMode() has been called.

:returns: REVLibError::kOk if successful

Set the maximum number of times to retry an RTR CAN frame. This applies
to calls such as SetParameter* and GetParameter* where a request is made
to the SPARK motor controller and a response is expected. Anytime sending
the request or receiving the response fails, it will retry the request a
number of times, no more than the value set by this method. If an attempt
succeeds, it will immediately return. The minimum number of retries is 0,
where only a single attempt will be made and will return regardless of
success or failure.

The default maximum is 5 retries.

:param num_retries: The maximum number of retries

Sets the timeout duration for waiting for CAN responses from the device.

:param milliseconds: The timeout in milliseconds.

Set the control frame send period for the native CAN Send thread. To
disable periodic sends, set periodMs to 0.

:param period_ms: The send period in milliseconds between 1ms and 100ms
                  or set to 0 to disable periodic sends. Note this is not updated until
                  the next call to Set() or SetReference().

Limits the current that the motor can draw, which protects the motor and keeps it from
    browning out the robot. This is REV's smart current limit, which only works with brushless
    motors. The default is 80 amps, which is too much for a NEO 550: 40 amps is common for a NEO
    and 20 amps for a NEO 550.

    :param amps: The most current the motor can draw, in amps.

Sets how the Spark Max calculates the velocity of the encoder, which get_encoder_velocity
    and set_velocity use. The velocity is the change in position over the measurement period,
    averaged over the last average_depth measurements. Smaller values make the velocity react
    faster but be noisier.

    :param average_depth:         How many measurements to average, from 1 to 64. The default
                                  is 8.
    :param measurement_period_ms: The time to measure the change in position over, in
                                  milliseconds, from 1 to 100. The default is 10.

Sets the feedforward gains that set_velocity and set_relative_position add to the PID
    output. Feedforward gives the motor the voltage that the target needs right away, so PID only
    has to fix what's left, which makes reaching a velocity much faster and steadier.

    :param s: The voltage it takes to start the motor moving, in volts.
    :param v: The voltage for each RPM of velocity, in volts per RPM.
    :param a: The voltage for each RPM per second of acceleration, in volts per RPM per second.
    :param slot: The closed loop slot to set it for, SLOT0 to SLOT3. set_velocity and
                 set_relative_position choose the slot to use.

Sets the voltage that holds an elevator up against gravity, which set_velocity and
    set_relative_position add to the PID output.

    :param g: The voltage it takes to hold the elevator still, in volts.
    :param slot: The closed loop slot to set it for, SLOT0 to SLOT3. set_velocity and
                 set_relative_position choose the slot to use.

Sets what the motor does when it is stopped: BRAKE holds it in place, COAST lets it spin
    freely.

    :param idle_mode: BRAKE or COAST.

Common interface for inverting direction of a speed controller.

This call has no effect if the controller is a follower. To invert
a follower, see the follow() method.

:deprecated: Use SparkBaseConfig.Inverted() with Configure() instead

:param is_inverted: The state of inversion, true is inverted.

Limits how hard set_velocity and set_relative_position can drive the motor, which is
    useful while tuning PID on a new mechanism. The default is -1 to 1.

    :param min_output: The lowest output, from -1 to 1.
    :param max_output: The highest output, from -1 to 1.
    :param slot:       The closed loop slot to set it for, SLOT0 to SLOT3. set_velocity and
                       set_relative_position choose the slot to use.

Set the amount of time to wait for a periodic status frame before
returning a timeout error. This timeout will apply to all periodic status
frames for the SPARK motor controller.

To prevent invalid timeout errors, the minimum timeout for a given
periodic status is 2.1 times its period. To use the minimum timeout for
all status frames, set timeoutMs to 0.

The default timeout is 500ms.

:param timeout_ms: The timeout in milliseconds

Sets the PID gains that set_velocity and set_relative_position use to reach their target.
    Each slot has its own gains, so a mechanism can switch between sets of gains, like one for
    moving and one for holding still.

    :param p:    The proportional gain.
    :param i:    The integral gain.
    :param d:    The derivative gain.
    :param slot: The closed loop slot to set the gains for, SLOT0 to SLOT3. set_velocity and
                 set_relative_position choose the slot to use.

Sets how long the motor takes to go from stopped to full power, so that it doesn't jerk.

    :param seconds: The time from stopped to full power, in seconds. 0 turns ramping off.

Changes the position that the encoder reports, without moving the motor. 0 zeroes it.

    :param position: The new position, in rotations.

Turns the motor to the given position, using the PID gains from set_pid.

    :param position: The position, in rotations, measured from where the encoder was zeroed.
    :param slot:     The closed loop slot whose gains and settings to use, SLOT0 to SLOT3.

Sets how close the motor has to be to the target of set_velocity or set_relative_position
    for is_at_setpoint to be true.

    :param tolerance: How close is close enough, in rotations for a position or RPM for a velocity.
    :param slot:      The closed loop slot to set it for, SLOT0 to SLOT3. set_velocity and
                      set_relative_position choose the slot to use.

Keeps the motor between two encoder positions, so that an arm or elevator can't be driven
    past the end of its travel. The Spark Max stops the motor itself, whatever the robot code
    tells it to do.

    :param reverse_limit: The lowest position, in rotations.
    :param forward_limit: The highest position, in rotations.

Sets the throttle of the motor controller.

:param throttle: The throttle where -1 indicates full reverse and 1
                 indicates full forward.

Spins the motor at the given speed, using the PID gains from set_pid.

    :param velocity: The speed, in rotations per minute.
    :param slot:     The closed loop slot whose gains and settings to use, SLOT0 to SLOT3.

Sets the voltage output of the SpeedController.  This is equivalent to
a call to SetReference(output, SparkBase::ControlType::kVoltage). The
behavior of this call differs slightly from the WPILib documentation for
this call since the device internally sets the desired voltage (not a
compensation value). That means that this *can* be a 'set-and-forget'
call.

:param output: The voltage to output.

Makes the motor run the same no matter how charged the battery is. Throttle and PID
    outputs are a fraction of the given voltage instead of a fraction of the battery voltage, so
    with 12 volts, a throttle of 0.5 is 6 volts. 12 volts is common.

    :param volts: The voltage that a throttle of 1.0 means, in volts. 0 turns voltage
                  compensation off.
Common interface to stop the motor until Set is called again.

instanceVariables.name: config_accessor
instanceVariables.tooltip:
Accessor for SPARK parameter values. This object contains fields and
methods to retrieve parameters that have been applied to the device. To
set parameters, see SparkBaseConfig and SparkBase::Configure.

NOTE: This uses calls that are blocking to retrieve parameters and should
be used infrequently.
